newsitem.title: USA: Crew arrives, countdown starts for Columbia flight.
newsitem.headline: Crew arrives, countdown starts for Columbia flight.

text.p: The crew of space shuttle Columbia arrived at Florida's Kennedy Space Centre on Monday as countdown clocks began ticking toward Thursday's blastoff.
Columbia, the oldest of NASA's four shuttles, is scheduled for launch at 2:01 p.m. EST (1901 GMT) on Thursday on a science research mission.
"Everything is coming together for a Thursday launch and we are just really looking forward to it," shuttle commander Jim Halsell said after arriving in Florida.
The weather forecast for Thursday's blastoff looked favourable, shuttle meteorologist Ed Priselac said. He gave the shuttle an 80 percent chance of getting off the launch pad.
Halsell and fellow astronauts Susan Still, Janice Voss, Don Thomas, Roger Crouch and Greg Linteris flew to Florida from their training base in Houston in T-38 training jets.

The seventh crew member, Mike Gernhardt, was recovering from a stomach bug and arrived later in another aircraft. NASA spokeswoman Eileen Hawley said he was expected to make a full recovery before Thursday's launch.
Still, a 35-year-old Naval aviator, was to become only the second woman to occupy the shuttle's co-pilot's seat. Crouch and Linteris are guest scientists who specialise in microgravity research.
The shuttle's three-day countdown began at 2 p.m. EST (1900 GMT). NASA officials said there were no technical problems facing the launch team.
The crew will be divided into two shifts to work around the clock in a European-built laboratory module, mounted in the shuttle's cargo bay.
During the 16-day mission the astronauts are to light dozens of fires inside a protective enclosure for combustion research, grow protein crystals and manufacture new materials.
